item.title: [39★] Quantum Dynamics of Dynamics
item.author: Takano Taira, Hiroyasu Tajima, Philip Taranto
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 39 ★

Authors: Takano Taira, Hiroyasu Tajima, Philip Taranto

arXiv ID: 2611.19265 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum channels (in discrete time) and Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) master equations (in continuous time) are the central tools of open quantum systems, but they rest on memoryless approximations (Born, Markov, secular) that fail in many physically relevant settings, most notably non-Markovian dynamics. There, tracking the state alone is insufficient: interventions at intermediate times disturb the environment, so multi-time correlations carry physical information that the state evolution cannot capture. The framework of higher-order quantum operations addresses this by treating controllable operations as \textitinputs to a process that maps operations to operations, so that the primitive object is a quantum \textitdynamics rather than a quantum \textitstate. Here, we derive the most general continuous-time, CP-divisible evolution of such an object, the \textitquantum comb master equation (QCME), which governs the quantum ``dynamics of dynamics''. Its GKSL-like generator includes encoder--decoder correlation terms coupling distinct temporal interventions. A generalized Born--Markov coarse-graining derivation identifies microscopic conditions for this structure. The QCME yields time-local evolution equations for two-time correlators beyond reduced-state dynamics and extends to more times. We show correlations between Schr"odinger- and Heisenberg-picture evolutions inaccessible to independent GKSL equations, describe quantum-channel evolution motivated by process tomography, and obtain time-local equations for linear response functions and OTOCs under environmental influences.

Takano Taira, Hiroyasu Tajima, Philip Taranto

item.title: [24★] Readout errors limit how far adaptive quantum circuits can entangle
item.author: Chenfeng Cao, Ruge Lin
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 24 ★

Authors: Chenfeng Cao, Ruge Lin

arXiv ID: 2611.20069 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Measurement and feedforward let quantum circuits entangle arbitrarily distant qubits in constant depth if measurement records are perfect and classical communication is instantaneous. We allow each reported bit to flip independently with a fixed probability between zero and one half, keeping all gates ideal. Consider a square-lattice device with a unique path between the endpoints and a bounded number of qubits per site. Beyond exp[O(D3)]exp[O(D3)]\exp[O(D^3)] steps along that path, every depth-DDD circuit starting from a product state leaves the endpoints exactly separable in every record, however rare. By copying outcomes onto spare qubits beside the path before readout, we attain a reach of exp[Θ(D3)]exp[Θ(D3)]\exp[\Theta(D^3)] for a nondestructive parity measurement at fixed accuracy without postselection. On a one-dimensional chain, the optimal reach for the same measurement is exp[Θ(D2)]exp[Θ(D2)]\exp[\Theta(D^2)]. On any interaction graph, a constant-depth circuit starting from a product state needs Ω(LlnL)Ω(LlnL)\Omega(L\ln L) qubits to entangle endpoints at graph distance LLL. The reliability of local readout thus limits the depth advantage of adaptive circuits for long-range entanglement.

Chenfeng Cao, Ruge Lin

item.title: [16★] Resolving and Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction
item.author: Alec Eickbusch, ..., Dmitry Abanin, et al (342)
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 16 ★

Authors: Alec Eickbusch, ..., Dmitry Abanin, et al (342)

arXiv ID: 2611.21578 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Scaling fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) requires suppressing errors in both space and time, yet standard logical memory experiments primarily probe spatial faults. Here, we use a 105-qubit Willow superconducting quantum processor to realize and scale the surface code stability experiment, which is alternatively sensitive to temporal error chains. Scaling from patch sizes of 3×33×33 \times 3 to 7×77×77 \times 7, we realize a timelike block suppression factor of μT=1.47±0.25μT=1.47±0.25\mu_T = 1.47 \pm 0.25, demonstrating the ability to maintain temporal error suppression as the number of qubits increases. By extending the stability experiment for many cycles, we uncover a sum-of-exponentials behavior in error suppression caused by a temporally correlated error: data-qubit heating to the third excited state |3⟩|3⟩|3\rangle. We fully capture this effect with a parameter-free, device-level leakage model incorporating higher-state transport during syndrome extraction cycles. To suppress this error, we develop and realize a walking stability circuit, reaching a logical error probability floor of ≤3.20×10−8≤3.20×10−8\le 3.20\times 10^{-8} at 60 cycles---two orders of magnitude below the standard construction---and limited by ionizing radiation error bursts. Finally, by adaptively terminating syndrome extraction based on decoder confidence in an offline analysis, we reduce spacetime logical error by 38% and time overhead by 34% compared to the optimal fixed-cycle strategy.

item.title: [16★] Optimal Quantum Sensing Algorithms for Discrete-Frequency Spectroscopy
item.author: Yu-Jie Liu, ..., Joonhee Choi, Soonwon Choi
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 16 ★

Authors: Yu-Jie Liu, ..., Joonhee Choi, Soonwon Choi

arXiv ID: 2611.21560 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Spectroscopy is a versatile tool that drives scientific discovery and underpins modern technologies. Quantum sensing offers promising opportunities to advance spectroscopy through enhanced sensitivity and spectral and spatial resolution. However, existing approaches largely focus on improving general measurement capabilities, often overlooking the structure of specific sensing tasks and leaving potential performance gains untapped. Here, we develop an algorithmic approach to quantum sensing tailored to various spectroscopic tasks, providing new avenues for improvement. Specifically, we consider general time-varying signals supported on a known set of NNN candidate frequencies, a setting we call discrete-frequency spectroscopy. We formulate three types of practically motivated sensing tasks---Detection, Search, and Learning---that require progressively more spectral information. For all tasks, we design optimal quantum sensing algorithms achieving a √NN−−√\sqrt{N} speedup over conventional frequency-scanning approaches. Optimal Detection and Search need only a single-qubit sensor under ππ\pi-pulse control, whereas optimal Learning provably requires coherent processing with a quantum computer. End-to-end numerical simulations incorporating various experimental imperfections predict up to two-orders-of-magnitude speedup in Detection. As an example, we analyze the feasibility of our Detection and Search algorithms for real-world molecular screening based on state-of-the-art nitrogen-vacancy centers. We also show how quantum-computing-enhanced Learning enables wireless communication in a weak-signal regime where conventional methods fail. Our results establish a practical route toward realizing quantum advantages via designing task-specific sensing algorithms.

Yu-Jie Liu, ..., Joonhee Choi, Soonwon Choi

item.title: [16★] TCBP-JOBS: GPU-Accelerated Quantum Error Correction Decoding and Noise Learning with Near-Optimal Accuracy
item.author: Ben Howe, ..., Kevin Young, Krysta M. Svore
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 16 ★

Authors: Ben Howe, ..., Kevin Young, Krysta M. Svore

arXiv ID: 2611.21321 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Achieving near-optimal quantum error correction (QEC) decoding accuracy often requires computationally expensive searches that limit both large-scale simulation and real-time operation. We introduce trajectory-calibrated belief propagation (TCBP), which learns calibrated fault probabilities from BP trajectories, and jittered OSD beam search (JOBS), which uses these probabilities to guide parallel GPU searches. Across surface, color and bivariate-bicycle code memory and surgery circuits, TCBP-JOBS achieves logical error rates comparable to those of the Tesseract most-likely-error decoder at physical error rates of 0.1% to 0.4%, and up to 4.5××\times lower on the largest codes. Serial speedups over Tesseract's sparsified presets range from 10××\times to 7,400××\times, and against unsparsified long-beam Tesseract they reach 13,000××\times on the bivariate-bicycle codes, at logical error rate ratios of 0.97 to 1.57. At lower physical error rates (10−410−410^{-4} to 5×10−45×10−45\times10^{-4}), rare-event splitting on the gross code shows that Tesseract is more accurate. Batched execution accelerates offline simulation for rapid, efficient exploration of large-scale QEC design spaces. For QPUs with longer logical clock cycles, our serial memory and logical-surgery experiments demonstrate accuracy comparable to Tesseract while meeting the millisecond-scale latency requirements of online feed-forward operation. Beyond memory and logic decoding, we demonstrate using TCBP-JOBS for confidence scores for postselection in memory and magic-state cultivation, enabling end-to-end color code cultivation. Together, these methods provide a GPU framework for accelerating QEC research via accurate decoding, noise estimation, and confidence assessment.

Ben Howe, ..., Kevin Young, Krysta M. Svore

item.title: [15★] Probing equilibrium properties with Gaussian states beyond mean-field
item.author: Esther Cruz, J. Ignacio Cirac, Dominik S. Wild
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 15 ★

Authors: Esther Cruz, J. Ignacio Cirac, Dominik S. Wild

arXiv ID: 2611.19313 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Computing equilibrium properties of interacting fermionic systems is central to many problems in condensed matter physics, yet computationally challenging. Mean-field methods tackle this problem by restricting to a tractable class of states, which, however, often fail to capture genuine many-body correlations. We illustrate this in the context of Gaussian mean-field methods by minimizing the energy variance of Gaussian states, showing that even states with the narrowest energy distributions poorly reproduce the microcanonical ensemble. To overcome this limitation, we develop a computationally efficient method to construct linear superpositions of Gaussian states whose energy variance can be systematically decreased by adding more terms to the superposition. We provide complementary results for the canonical ensemble, for which we propose a sampling algorithm based on convex combinations of Gaussian states. We benchmark our methods using the ttt--VVV model and find that both methods greatly outperform mean-field calculations. In particular, we obtain the correct critical exponents as well as a significantly improved estimate for the critical temperature. As an independent result, we prove a quantum Berry--Esseen theorem for fermionic Gaussian states, which states that the local density of states converges to a Gaussian distribution in the thermodynamic limit without any assumptions about the spatial correlations of the state.

Esther Cruz, J. Ignacio Cirac, Dominik S. Wild

item.title: [15★] Double-Randomized Quantum Singular Value Transformations For Early Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers
item.author: Joel Bierman, Pawan Poudel, Yuan Liu
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 15 ★

Authors: Joel Bierman, Pawan Poudel, Yuan Liu

arXiv ID: 2611.18881 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT) is an algorithmic framework which encompasses a wide range of problems, including Hamiltonian dynamics, ground state preparation, Gibbs state preparation, amplitude amplification, and matrix inversion. For many areas of scientific interest such as quantum chemistry and condensed matter, the circuit depth of the block-encoding subroutine in QSVT can be formidable, limiting the scope of problems to which QSVT can be applied on early fault-tolerant hardware. We split linear operators AAA into a core operator A0A0A_0 and a tail operator AϵAϵA_\epsilon, block-encoding the normalized sum of A0A0A_0 and the average of nTnTn_T randomly sampled terms from AϵAϵA_\epsilon. We show that using randomized block-encodings of this form allows one to lower the circuit depth of QSVT while incurring a diamond norm error that scales as O(CPδ2/nTO(CPδ2/nT\mathcal{O}(C_P\delta^2/n_T), where CPCPC_P is a prefactor which depends on the QSVT polynomial PPP and δδ\delta is the ratio of the ℓ1ℓ1\ell_1 norms of the coefficient vectors of AϵAϵA_\epsilon and AAA. We then go on to show that if one samples QSVT circuits from a joint probability distribution of both random block-encodings and random polynomials (Double-Randomized QSVT), then the circuit depth savings of these two randomization techniques combine multiplicatively, with only additive error contributions. We numerically calculate error bounds for long-range Heisenberg and iron-sulfur complex Hamiltonians, showing that for a diamond norm error bound of 10−310−310^{-3}, RBE-QSVT can reduce the number of Pauli terms needed for the block-encoding by an order of magnitude or more in several cases. This paves the way for demonstrations of QSVT on early fault-tolerant hardware.

Joel Bierman, Pawan Poudel, Yuan Liu

item.title: [14★] Accurate qLDPC decoding under real-time constraints
item.author: Chenzewei Qing, ..., Xiaolu Su, Li You
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 14 ★

Authors: Chenzewei Qing, ..., Xiaolu Su, Li You

arXiv ID: 2611.19130 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires reconciling the computational demands of accurate decoding with the stringent timing constraints of real-time error correction. We present Spatiotemporal Covariance-Optimized Parallel Ensemble (SCOPE), a physics-informed framework for real-time decoding of quantum low-density parity-check codes (qLDPC). By exploiting the spatial symmetries of bivariate-bicycle (BB) codes and the temporal regularity of repeated syndrome extraction, SCOPE uncovers a spatiotemporally covariant decoding structure and organizes the circuit-level problem into a layered decoding strategy. We further compress the high-dimensional evolution of belief propagation (BP) into a low-dimensional dynamical representation, revealing distinct signatures of successful and failed decoding and enabling early detection of unpromising trajectories. Guided by these dynamical signatures, SCOPE explores multiple perturbed decoding trajectories in parallel, enabling early termination and reseeding within a fixed serial iteration budget, with message-passing parameters optimized offline by simulated annealing. Circuit-level simulations of the [[144,12,12]][[144,12,12]][[144,12,12]] BB code yield a logical error rate of pL=4.82×10−10pL=4.82×10−10p_L=4.82\times10^{-10} at a physical error rate of p=10−3p=10−3p=10^{-3}. We further realize a pipelined two-arm memory-augmented BP (Mem-BP) core at the register-transfer level. Functional simulations at a 250 MHz clock yield a 16 ns BP iteration interval per arm and a mean input-to-result latency of 173.8 ns at p=5×10−3p=5×10−3p=5\times10^{-3}.

item.title: [14★] A Quasipolynomial Quantum Algorithm for the Vector Dihedral Coset Problem with Smooth Modulus
item.author: Aparna Gupte
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 14 ★

Authors: Aparna Gupte

arXiv ID: 2611.18857 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We give a quantum algorithm for the vector dihedral coset problem over Znq\mathbb{Z}_q^n, in which the goal is to recover s∈Znq\mathbf{s} \in \mathbb{Z}_q^n given independent samples of the form 1√2(|0,x⟩+|1,x+s⟩)\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bigl(|{0,\mathbf{x}}\rangle+|{1,\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{s}}\rangle\bigr), for x∼Znq\mathbf{x}\sim \mathbb{Z}_q^n. When the modulus qq is BB-smooth, the algorithm uses nO(B1+o(1)logq)BO(B2+o(1)logq)n^{O(B^{1+o(1)}\log q)}B^{O(B^{2+o(1)}\log q)} samples and time. For B=polylog(n)B = \mathrm{polylog}(n) and q=poly(n)q=\mathrm{poly}(n), this gives a quasipolynomial time- and sample-complexity. This extends the previously known quasipolynomial-time result for power-of-two moduli (Bonnetain, Naya-Plasencia, ASIACRYPT 2018; Bai, Jangir, Kirshanova, Ngo, Youmans, CRYPTO 2025). The algorithm proceeds by reducing the modulus one prime factor p|qp | q at a time. The key ingredient is a sieving procedure that clears the non-linear terms in the phase modulo pp via an algorithm of Ivanyos, Santha (TCS 2017) that finds non-zero u∈Fℓp\mathbf{u} \in \mathbb{F}_p^\ell such that ∑i∈[ℓ]udiai=0modp\sum_{i \in [\ell]} u_i^d \mathbf{a}_i = 0 \mod p for degrees 1≤d≤p−11 \le d \le p-1, given vectors a1,…,aℓ∈Fnp\mathbf{a}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{a}_\ell \in \mathbb{F}_p^n as input. The algorithm also applies to the extrapolated dihedral coset problem (EDCP) introduced by Brakerski, Kirshanova, Stehlé, Wen (PKC 2018), which is known to be equivalent to LWE in the polynomial sample regime. However, our result does not yield a new attack on LWE in any regime, precisely because the known reduction from LWE to EDCP provides only polynomially many clean samples, whereas our algorithm requires quasipolynomially many samples. The main algorithm was obtained in a GPT-5.6 Sol conversation prompted by the author; the author is responsible for all statements, proofs, and correctness. Concurrent work of Boucher, Fouque, Shen gives an algorithm with similar guarantees for prime-power moduli.

Abstract:

item.title: [8★] Rate-1/2 Quantum LDPC Codes for Multi-tier Superconducting Hardware
item.author: Jiaxuan Zhang, ..., Yu-Chun Wu, Guo-Ping Guo
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 8 ★

Authors: Jiaxuan Zhang, ..., Yu-Chun Wu, Guo-Ping Guo

arXiv ID: 2611.20410 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum error correction is essential for scalable quantum computing, while its resource overhead is governed in large part by the encoding rate, namely the number of logical qubits encoded per physical data qubit. Recent quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) constructions have entered the ultra-high-rate regime with encoding rates above 1/2, but their syndrome-extraction circuits generally rely on reconfigurable connectivity or long-range qubit transport, making them difficult to implement on fixed-connectivity superconducting hardware. Here we introduce Armillary codes, a family of ultra-high-rate qLDPC codes whose algebraic structure is generated by native iSWAP routing under hardware constraints. The construction jointly enforces stabilizer commutation and correct parallel syndrome extraction, while admitting radial and circumferential couplings in crossing-free routing layers. We construct explicit codes with rates above 1/2, stabilizer weight 12, Tanner-graph girth 6, and distances from 12 to 16, with layouts on 5 or 6 hardware tiers. Compared with the Gross and Mitten codes at the same distances, the Armillary codes achieve encoding rates about 6 and 2.5 times those of the Gross and Mitten codes, respectively, while maintaining lower hardware-complexity scores. In circuit-level simulations, the [[8688,4348,16]][\![8688,4348,16]\!]code approaches the teraquop regime, achieving a logical error rate of 1.62×10−121.62\times10^-12per logical qubit per round at a physical error rate of 0.1\%. These results show that the rate-1/21/2regime of qLDPC codes can be extended from reconfigurable platforms to superconducting hardware, providing a route toward low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum processors.

Jiaxuan Zhang, ..., Yu-Chun Wu, Guo-Ping Guo

item.title: [8★] Linear-optical nonlocality without postselection
item.author: Daniel J. Brod, Ernesto F. Galvão
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 8 ★

Authors: Daniel J. Brod, Ernesto F. Galvão

arXiv ID: 2611.19570 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Linear optics is one of the major platforms for quantum information processing and experimental tests of quantum foundations. This motivates a thorough exploration of its capabilities and limitations. In this paper we investigate the extent to which passive linear optics, when fed with single-photon Fock states and followed by postselection-free number-resolving measurements, can demonstrate nonlocality. These resources define BosonSampling, a computational model believed to have intermediate computational power, being neither classically simulable nor quantum universal. We prove that, when restricted to only two input photons, this system also has intermediate nonlocality capabilities, achieving a violation of the CHSH inequality no higher than 1+√21+\sqrt{2}. Although this value has appeared frequently in the literature as achievable, to our knowledge this is the first proof that it is maximal. We show that, as we increase the number of available photons, linear optics can produce violations arbitrarily close to Tsirelson's bound of 2√22\sqrt{2}. Finally, we extend the analysis to tripartite nonlocality, leveraging well-known interferometric suppression laws to show how several tripartite inequalities can be violated in this setup beyond their bipartite bounds.

Daniel J. Brod, Ernesto F. Galvão

item.title: [8★] Witnessing Magic (and other Quantum Resources)
item.author: Brian Barch, Luis Pedro García-Pintos
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 8 ★

Authors: Brian Barch, Luis Pedro García-Pintos

arXiv ID: 2611.19017 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Motivated by measurements of quantum magic, we study the sampling cost of resource robustness ---a quantifier for a broad class of quantum resources--- by bounding the variance of optimal robustness witnesses. We first lower bound the samples required to estimate a state's resource robustness using Cramér-Rao bounds. We find that the number of measurements scales at least quadratically in the robustness for highly mixed states, and at least linearly in the generalized robustness for broad families of pure states, making it difficult to measure either robustness to low absolute error when the states are highly resourceful. We then derive two complementary bounds in terms of the geometry of witnesses, one of which is tight for a class of resource theories including coherence and bipartite entanglement. An additional hurdle occurs for tracking the onset of resource robustness along state-space trajectories: the integrated witness variance along a path is at least the squared resource gain over Fisher length, indicating that a state evolution with exponential resource gain necessarily goes through states for which the robustness cannot be measured efficiently. This hurdle does not occur when estimating robustness to fixed relative, rather than absolute, error. These results suggest that the ideal witness-based resource estimation task, for general resource theories, is the estimation of generalized robustness to low relative error on highly resourceful pure states.

Brian Barch, Luis Pedro García-Pintos

item.title: [7★] Static Bounds on Thermal Fast Scrambling
item.author: Yixuan Ma, Weikang Li, Dong-Ling Deng
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 7 ★

Authors: Yixuan Ma, Weikang Li, Dong-Ling Deng

arXiv ID: 2611.20958 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Scrambling, the process by which initially localized quantum information spreads across an interacting many-body system, is a hallmark of quantum chaos and plays a central role in understanding black hole dynamics. In thermal systems, the chaos bound of Maldacena, Shenker and Stanford limits the exponential growth rate of out-of-time-order correlations to 2π/β2\pi/\beta, assuming that time-ordered correlation functions factorize after a dissipation time. Establishing the corresponding rigorous logarithmic lower bounds on scrambling times at arbitrary fixed temperature has remained an open problem, most notably in disordered systems, where the Gibbs state depends on the same random couplings that drive the dynamics. Here we prove such bounds at every fixed temperature for the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model and for random kk-local spin systems, without assuming real-time factorization. Our approach uses the operator-size distribution of the square root of the Gibbs state to quantify how local probes modify its structure. This static information bounds the thermal correlator uniformly in time along the edges of its analytic strip in complex time, and analyticity then limits how rapidly scrambling can develop. For both families of models, we prove that with probability tending to one the scrambling time is at least (1−ϵ)[β/(2π)]logN(1-\epsilon)[\beta/(2\pi)]\log N for any 0<ϵ<10<\epsilon<1, with the coefficient β/(2π)\beta/(2\pi) suggested by the chaos bound. The bound holds for each fixed pair of distinct Majorana modes in the SYK model and for the target average of any fixed single-site source in the spin model. These results place the thermal fast-scrambling timescale on a rigorous footing and show how static properties of the Gibbs state can constrain real-time information spreading.

Yixuan Ma, Weikang Li, Dong-Ling Deng

item.title: [7★] Efficient XXXX Placement Strategies for Energy-Gap Enhancement in Quantum Annealing
item.author: Jennivine Chen, Natasha Feinstein, P A Warburton
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 7 ★

Authors: Jennivine Chen, Natasha Feinstein, P A Warburton

arXiv ID: 2611.20902 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum annealing offers the prospect of a computational advantage over classical methods for certain classes of combinatorial optimisation problems. Its performance, however, is fundamentally constrained by the minimum spectral gap between the ground state and the first excited state encountered during the annealing process. When this gap closes exponentially with problem size, the runtime required to maintain adiabatic evolution can likewise grow exponentially, severely limiting the practical efficiency of the annealer. For problems including the maximum weight independent set (MWIS), previous work has shown that introducing XXXX interactions along problem-graph edges can substantially enlarge the minimum energy-gap and thereby improve annealing performance. In practice, however, current quantum annealing hardware does not support these interactions natively and methods for implementing effective XXXX couplings come with hardware overhead and connectivity constraints. These limitations motivate the use of only a limited number of XXXX interactions. In this paper, we investigate XXXX placement strategies for MWIS instances under both resource and topological constraints, and demonstrate that careful selection of the placements can substantially increase the minimum energy-gap. We evaluate these strategies through a detailed statistical analysis of both deliberately constructed hard MWIS instances and random Erdős--Rényi graphs. Notably, these strategies are particularly effective for hard MWIS instances with initially small minimum gaps, where targeted placement yields the largest relative improvements.

Jennivine Chen, Natasha Feinstein, P A Warburton

item.title: [6★] Specifying & Verifying Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
item.author: Stavan Jain, Nithin Raveendran, Aws Albarghouthi
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 6 ★

Authors: Stavan Jain, Nithin Raveendran, Aws Albarghouthi

arXiv ID: 2611.21236 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Building quantum computers is challenging due to the noise that affects qubits. Quantum error correction tackles noise by encoding information in quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes. These codes are often complex, increasingly found by computational search, presented in diverse formalisms with informal arguments, and hard to reason about algorithmically. Given that the rest of the quantum computing stack relies on a QEC code's properties for correct computation, we propose a formally verified foundation for QEC codes. We present QECLean, a Lean-based framework for formally specifying and verifying QEC codes. QECLean backs every claimed QEC-code property with a machine-checked proof, unifies the diverse presentations of codes in the literature through common abstractions, and makes new codes easy to specify. We present a new compositional technique, code combinators, for proving code distance analytically. Code combinators allow us to prove the distance of large codes that are out of reach for algorithmic techniques; for example, we show that IBM's [[360,12,≤24]][[360, 12, \leq 24]] code has distance 24, which was previously only known as an upper bound. Furthermore, we show how our approach allows us to formalize and prove entire code families, such as the surface code. Our work lays the foundation required for reasoning about circuit-level implementations of codes on given architectures and for building end-to-end verified compilers for quantum computers. QECLean is available at https://github.com/Stavan-Jain/QECLean

Stavan Jain, Nithin Raveendran, Aws Albarghouthi

item.title: [6★] Randomized routing: ruling out classical networks without trusting source independence
item.author: Martin Plávala
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 6 ★

Authors: Martin Plávala

arXiv ID: 2611.20866 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Network nonlocality without inputs assumes that the sources are independent, but no data can test this, since one classical source feeding all parties reproduces any correlation. Here we propose a randomized routing strategy: a source is duplicated, and the two parties it connects choose at random which copy to read. Whether any classical network, even with correlated sources, explains the routed data is then a linear program, and its infeasibility certificates are linear inequalities on the data. Source independence is thus traded for locality and free choice of the routing, which experiments can enforce. In the triangle scenario, the RGB4 distribution fails the test over a wide range of parameters, including a point where its triangle data alone have a numerically found model with independent classical sources, and it still fails with 3\% white noise at each source.

Martin Plávala

item.title: [5★] Vanishing Relative Distance of Uniformly Random CSS LDPC Codes Built from Permutation Matrices
item.author: Kenta Kasai
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 5 ★

Authors: Kenta Kasai

arXiv ID: 2611.21389 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Classical random regular low-density parity-check codes can have minimum distance growing linearly with block length. We study CSS check matrices formed as full J×LJ\times L arrays of arbitrary P×PP\times P permutation matrices, sampled uniformly subject to commutation. For fixed column weight J≥3J\ge3 and fixed even row weight L>2JL>2J, we prove that the relative minimum distance converges to zero in probability as P→∞P\to\infty, with block length n=LPn=LP. We analyze the weight enumerators that count all nontrivial logical representatives after excluding stabilizers. A coefficientwise lower bound shows that, at every fixed relative weight 0<α<10<\alpha<1 along even-weight sequences, exponentially many such representatives exist with high probability. Their typical and mean counts have exponent lower bound h2(α)/2h_2(\alpha)/2, where h2h_2 is the binary entropy function. We compare this bound with the classical LDPC and dense CSS mean weight-distribution exponents. The existence, with high probability, of a logical operator below every fixed target weight δn\delta n yields the distance conclusion.

item.title: [5★] Closing the loop on memory: accurate, shallow and transferable decoding of quantum LDPC codes
item.author: Zhou You, ..., Xiao Yuan, Yuan Yao
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 5 ★

Authors: Zhou You, ..., Xiao Yuan, Yuan Yao

arXiv ID: 2611.21086 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes have attracted interest for fault-tolerant quantum computing because their high-rate constructions offer a route to reduced qubit overhead. Realizing this potential requires reliable decoding. Belief propagation (BP) forms the basis of many qLDPC decoders, but can fail to converge under circuit-level noise. Memory-based variants can improve convergence, yet selecting memory strengths that work reliably across different syndromes remains challenging. Here we introduce TEMPO-BP, which adapts each variable's memory strength to the evolving decoding state through local feedback. On the gross code at a physical error rate of 0.4%, single-run TEMPO-BP achieves a per-shot logical failure rate of 0.73%, compared with 2.51% for BP+OSD+CS-10. Ensembles of 10-15 concurrent instances match or lower failure counts relative to Relay-BP-5 at all ten tested operating points, with per-instance iteration caps at least tenfold lower than its serial limit. Without retuning, the gross-code parameters yield fewer observed failures than Relay-BP-5 in its published gross-code configuration across four additional code families. Ablations support state-dependent memory control, while a loop-gain analysis characterizes specific amplification modes in the decoding dynamics.

Zhou You, ..., Xiao Yuan, Yuan Yao

item.title: [5★] Formally verified harness for Shor's order finding algorithm with O(n2+ϵ)O(n^{2+\epsilon}) gate cost
item.author: Anirudh Suresh, ..., Runzhou Tao, Yudong Cao
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 5 ★

Authors: Anirudh Suresh, ..., Runzhou Tao, Yudong Cao

arXiv ID: 2611.20342 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

It is commonly understood that factoring a general nn-bit biprime via Shor's order finding algorithm requires ˜O(n3)\widetilde{O}(n^3) gates by leveraging schoolbook integer arithmetics for addition and multiplication. Recent developments in quantum arithmetic circuits leveraging recursive Toom-Cook schemes have improved the cost scaling to O(n2+ϵ)O(n^{2+\epsilon}). Here ϵ>0\epsilon>0 depends on algorithm implementation details of the recursive multiplication steps, which allow for a vast number of design choices. The challenge in navigating such design space also presents an opportunity for demonstrating innovative practices in quantum software engineering in the era of open agentic science. We present a formally verified harness that ingests a design specification (namely a "policy" that describes a recursive circuit design scheme) from an external source, which may be an AI agent, and produces a set of formalized proofs covering mathematical correctness of the algorithm implementation, asymptotic scaling of the end-to-end gate cost, as well as the correctness of translating the verified algorithm to a detailed circuit implementation with an intermediate representation. The harness is published as an open challenge where human researchers and AI agents can search for more efficient factoring circuits while retaining machine-checked guarantees of correctness and end-to-end asymptotic complexity.

item.title: [5★] Universal Quantum Computation in a Wigner's Friend Framework
item.author: Martí Cladera-Rosselló, ..., Lee A. Rozema, Philip Walther
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 5 ★

Authors: Martí Cladera-Rosselló, ..., Lee A. Rozema, Philip Walther

arXiv ID: 2611.18839 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The Wigner's Friend thought experiment illustrates a core tension in quantum mechanics: an observer inside an isolated laboratory (the Friend) measures a definite outcome, while an external observer (Wigner) describes the laboratory as a coherent superposition. Here we show that this discrepancy, usually studied as a conflict between descriptions, has a direct computational consequence. We namely propose a protocol by which Wigner can turn the Friend's laboratory into a universal quantum computer, whereby the Friend is restricted to apply simple classical operations within the laboratory. We also experimentally implement a proof-of-principle demonstration of this protocol for single-qubit gates using single photons. By recasting the coherence between incompatible descriptions as a computational resource, we thus link the foundations of quantum measurement to quantum computation.

Martí Cladera-Rosselló, ..., Lee A. Rozema, Philip Walther

item.title: [4★] Proxima: Optimizing Syndrome Extraction Circuit Scheduling for Practical Quantum LDPC Codes
item.author: Ruiyun Zhang, ..., Jun Xia, Yuan Xie
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 4 ★

Authors: Ruiyun Zhang, ..., Jun Xia, Yuan Xie

arXiv ID: 2611.19715 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The fault-tolerant performance of quantum error correction codes relies critically on the scheduling of parity checks in syndrome extraction circuits (SECs). For general CSS-type quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, the vast scheduling space and intricate error-propagation patterns make it computationally prohibitive to directly optimize the logical error rate (LER) or the exact circuit-level distance (dcircd_{\mathrm{circ}}). To address this challenge, we introduce Proxima, a highly effective automated SEC scheduling framework guided by a distance-related metric termed proximity. Defined directly on the detector error model (DEM), proximity quantifies the minimum number of additional faults required to complete a seed fault to an undetectable logical failure, naturally capturing arbitrary circuit-level fault mechanisms and bounding dcircd_{\mathrm{circ}} from above. Proxima synthesizes a pool of valid schedules at a target depth and ranks them by evaluating proximity within small, graph-local DEM fault subsets, progressively enlarging the subset only to break ties among top-ranked candidates. Across a broad spectrum of qLDPC code families, Proxima consistently attains low circuit depths and high circuit-level distance bounds, reducing LER by 1.4--2.6×\times over the strongest automated baseline and up to 40×40\times over others while generalizing robustly across noise models and decoders. Furthermore, by exploiting translational symmetry via a compact monomial representation, Proxima discovers depth-8 uniform schedules for bivariate bicycle codes that surpass even IBM's depth-7 reference schedule [Nature, 2024] by 2.1--5.1×\times, establishing the DEM-level proximity as a practical objective for fault-tolerant compilation.

Ruiyun Zhang, ..., Jun Xia, Yuan Xie

item.title: [3★] Plenitude of ideal correlations explains quantum theory
item.author: Adán Cabello
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Adán Cabello

arXiv ID: 2611.21448 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We show that the Hilbert-space formalism and the Born rule of quantum theory are singled out by the following principle: every correlation that is possible in a theory in which every observable admits an ideal measurement is physically realizable. An ideal measurement is one that yields the same outcome when repeated and does not disturb any compatible observable.

Adán Cabello

item.title: [3★] Information Causality Defeats Every Finite NPA Level
item.author: Anubhav Chaturvedi, Marcin Pawłowski
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Anubhav Chaturvedi, Marcin Pawłowski

arXiv ID: 2611.21371 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

For every finite level of the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy, we construct correlations that satisfy all its constraints but violate information causality. At each fixed level, one use of a binary-outcome correlation and one classical bit suffice for a violation that grows without bound as the number of measurement settings increases. Information causality bounds the information gained about independent database bits, summed over possible requests, by the length of the message. Quantum correlations obey the one-bit bound; the optimal information gain at any fixed NPA level grows logarithmically with the number of settings. The violation remains unbounded even when all outcome probabilities are positive and, for any fixed number of measurement settings on each side, every choice of those settings admits a local model. One communicated bit therefore exposes an unbounded gap between information causality and every finite NPA level.

Anubhav Chaturvedi, Marcin Pawłowski

item.title: [3★] No complete set of mutually unbiased bases in C^6 without Fourier vanishing
item.author: Jinze Yang, ..., Yangyang Li, Xiu-Hao Deng
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Jinze Yang, ..., Yangyang Li, Xiu-Hao Deng

arXiv ID: 2611.19809 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

A recent exact certificate shows that C^6 admits no seven mutually unbiased bases, hence at most five (OpenAI, 2026). That argument has two parts. The first proves the Fourier-vanishing conjecture of Matolcsi, Ruzsa and Weiner for every complex Hadamard matrix of order six other than Tao's cubic matrix, and excludes the cubic matrix separately. The second feeds this vanishing into a positivity certificate on mixed moments of a hypothetical complete family. We show that the first part is not needed. We keep the same six families of test functions and the same linear identities, but we never set a moment to zero because of Fourier vanishing. New positive definite integer matrices still give the contradiction. The only inputs are orthonormality, unbiasedness, the second-moment (2-design) identity of a complete family, and the trivial bound |moment| <= 1. A standard-library program checks the certificate in exact integer and rational arithmetic in under a minute and a half. We also record computational observations that are not part of the proof: a systematic S_6-symmetric family of test functions appears to close the argument with relations of total order at most 7 instead of 11, and at order 9 two orbit types of test charges appear to suffice. In the prime-power dimensions 4,5,7,8, where complete families exist, the same pipeline finds no certificate, as it must.

Jinze Yang, ..., Yangyang Li, Xiu-Hao Deng

item.title: [3★] Fragmentation in Non-Hermitian Many-Body Systems
item.author: Stefano Longhi
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Stefano Longhi

arXiv ID: 2611.19205 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

In non-Hermitian (NH) fermionic chains with spatially random imaginary gauge fields, single-particle eigenstates exhibit erratic NH skin localization with strongly fluctuating, subexponential decay, distinct from both conventional skin accumulation and Anderson localization. At finite filling, Pauli exclusion suppresses macroscopic accumulation and instead leads to fragmentation of the particle density, in sharp contrast to Hermitian disordered systems. Using exact free-fermion methods, we show that the density organizes into disconnected regions of high and low occupancy, forming spatially separated Fermi domains whose number NFSN_{\mathrm{FS}} scales subextensively with system size LL. Remarkably, fragmentation is not only an equilibrium property but also emerges dynamically in the NH evolution, unlike in Hermitian systems where such structures are not dynamically selected. This behavior admits a Coulomb-gas description in a stochastic potential, establishing a direct link between erratic NH skin localization and real-space fragmentation of many-body states.

Stefano Longhi

item.title: [3★] Metamorphic Testing of Quantum Software based on Stabilizer States
item.author: Adrián Marín Boyero, ..., Otfried Gühne, Malte Lochau
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Adrián Marín Boyero, ..., Otfried Gühne, Malte Lochau

arXiv ID: 2611.18838 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

A major challenge in quantum computing is to systematically check if a quantum program implements its desired functionality. For classical programs, testing is widely used; each test case comprises a pair of sample input and expected output to be compared with the actual output. To increase the number of test cases, however, one has to solve the test-oracle problem: for each additional test input one has to know the correct output. Metamorphic testing tackles this problem by utilizing metamorphic relations between input and output domains to automatically derive new test cases from existing ones. However, adapting metamorphic testing to the quantum realm is not straightforward, since quantum states cannot be directly inspected. We propose a framework of quantum metamorphic testing (QMT) in which the metamorphic relations incorporate the measurement procedures required to assess quantum outputs. We apply our QMT framework to testing the preparation of stabilizer states, which are central to protocols like measurement-based quantum computing or quantum error correction. We utilize structural properties of stabilizer states to systematically derive measurement circuits for new test cases from existing ones. We implement this framework in Qiskit, and demonstrate that it reduces by an order of magnitude the testing run time compared to testing with randomly generated input states. We further show effectiveness by revealing synthetic program faults injected by circuit mutations, as well as a real bug in the Qiskit compiler.

Adrián Marín Boyero, ..., Otfried Gühne, Malte Lochau

item.title: [2★] Stabilizer-Restricted Antidistinguishability in Quantum Computation with Magic States
item.author: Selman Ipek
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Selman Ipek

arXiv ID: 2611.21123 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

An antidistinguishing measurement for a family of preparations excludes at least one preparation for every possible outcome, constraining 'classical' representations of these processes, known as ontological models. We develop this connection within quantum computing with magic states (QCM), a universal model of quantum computation. Our constructions use adaptive Pauli measurements on tensor products of single-qubit non stabilizer states, including families associated with the Clifford hierarchy. These constructions yield stabilizer-restricted versions of the Pusey-Barrett-Rudolph theorem: any ontological model reproducing these measurement statistics and satisfying preparation independence must assign disjoint ontic supports to the preparations considered. We demonstrate this obstruction to preparation independence in a concrete ontological model based on convex polytopes used for the classical simulation of QCM.

Selman Ipek

item.title: [2★] Quantum Sensing of Defects
item.author: Simone Cavazzoni, ..., Matteo G.A. Paris, Abolfazl Bayat
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Simone Cavazzoni, ..., Matteo G.A. Paris, Abolfazl Bayat

arXiv ID: 2611.20509 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Metrology of defects (or impurities) is a major challenge in quantum sensing, with implications for material science, nano-scale metrology, and the development of high-precision quantum devices. In this work, we employ single and multi excitation sensors for the metrology of defects, with the system Hamiltonian encoding the structure of the sensor and the defect treated as a perturbation potential. We evaluate the quantum Fisher information of the ground state of the system to quantify the metrological performance of the sensors in locating a defect and in estimating its coupling strength. In doing so, we identify two distinct sensing regimes, determined by the ratio between the defect screening parameter and the inter-sensor site spacing, and establish the scaling behavior for the resulting estimation precision. Furthermore, we analyze the joint estimation of defect position and strength as well as the performance of two-excitation sensors, demonstrating how the number of excitations and their interactions influence sensitivity. Our results provide tools for optimizing defect detection with quantum sensors, with potential applications in solid-state quantum technologies.

Simone Cavazzoni, ..., Matteo G.A. Paris, Abolfazl Bayat

item.title: [2★] Quantum Loading of Charge and Spin-Adapted MPS
item.author: Matthew R. Hennefarth, ..., Sukin Sim, Modjtaba Shokrian Zini
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Matthew R. Hennefarth, ..., Sukin Sim, Modjtaba Shokrian Zini

arXiv ID: 2611.19728 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Matrix product states (MPS) are powerful classical representations of correlated quantum states, but loading a large bond dimension MPS can substantially increase the cost in fault-tolerant quantum algorithms. We develop a circuit for preparing a U(1)~×\times~SU(2)-symmetric MPS directly from spin-adapted reduced tensors. Using Householder--LKS synthesis, the circuit prepares each symmetry-allowed reduced block and applies Clebsch--Gordan coefficients to recover the magnetic degrees of freedom, avoiding explicit loading of the corresponding unfolded dense tensors. The reduced-tensor data loading is dominant in cost. We benchmark 4×44 \times 4 and 4×64 \times 6 Fermi--Hubbard states and active-space models of \ce[Fe2S2]^2-, \ce[Fe4S4]^2-, and low- and high-spin cytochrome P450. At 15-bit rotation precision, the molecular benchmarks show ∼14×\sim 14\times to 54×54\times Toffoli reductions, ∼20×\sim 20\times to 87×87\times active volume reduction, and ∼33×\sim 33\times to 140×140\times volume (Toffoli ×\times qubits) reduction at the QROM-optimal point, relative to dense MPS loading. Fermi--Hubbard speedups increase with bond dimension and track the inverse tensor density, with modest qubit overhead. However, while we discuss generalization of our algorithm to reduce cost given further symmetry or using more performant unitary synthesis methods, extrapolation to larger lattices suggests that DMRG-state loading may exceed downstream phase-estimation costs, motivating co-design of state fidelity, compression, and the initial-state ansatz.

Abstract:

We study the depth of CZ circuits, Clifford state preparation, and Clifford unitary synthesis over the two-dimensional square lattice. A programmable circuit on a 2×k2{\times}k ladder (n=2kn{=}2k) implements an arbitrary CZ computation in depth at most 3n2+3\frac{3n}{2}{+}3 up to reversal of both rails. item.title: [2★] A Numerical Approach to Quantization
item.author: Grace Murray, ..., Ioannis G. Kevrekidis, Trung V. Phan
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Grace Murray, ..., Ioannis G. Kevrekidis, Trung V. Phan

arXiv ID: 2611.19646 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We introduce a numerical approach that simultaneously searches for matrix quantizations and compatible Poisson structures on classical geometric surfaces. Our method identifies irreducible Hermitian matrix representations and a trainable Poisson multiplier by minimizing a loss function that penalizes violations of the Casimir and commutation constraints. Through numerical investigations and subsequent theoretical analysis, we establish a no-go theorem showing that, for Weyl quantized fuzzy spheres with nondegenerate axial spectrum, the matrix dimension cannot exceed the degree of the nonconstant polynomial axial Poisson multiplier. We further extend our approach to nonpolynomial Poisson multipliers, demonstrating its versatility and potential to drive novel discoveries. Although here we focus on Weyl quantized fuzzy spheres, the framework is extensible to general geometric manifolds and quantization schemes. Our approach also provides a practical starting point for investigating Schild string theory and the quantization of spacetime histories.

item.title: [2★] A Universal Algebraic Construction of Hilbert-Space Fragmentation
item.author: Pramod Padmanabhan, Vladimir Korepin
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Pramod Padmanabhan, Vladimir Korepin

arXiv ID: 2611.19470 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We present a mechanism for obtaining Hilbert-space fragmentation from arbitrary quantum lattice Hamiltonians acting on finite-dimensional local spaces. We first express the Hamiltonian in an algebraic form using supersymmetry (SUSY) and parasupersymmetry (paraSUSY) generators. Enlarging their representations defines a lifting procedure, which we study in two forms, site-wise and bond-wise lifting. Site-wise lifting introduces immobile zero modes that generate exponentially many invariant sectors while retaining the original dynamics in the fully active sector. We determine the sector structure and establish strong fragmentation for uniform lifts at fixed intermediate zero-mode density. For nearest-neighbor chains, correlation functions reveal restricted propagation and, in the mixed-field example, persistent local memory. Bond-wise lifting produces mobile conserved strings, pair-flip dynamics and fluctuating dimers, and extends to fragmented unitary circuits. Different representations and embeddings realize different fragmentation mechanisms. Some of the fragmented models obtained by this method include lifted permutation and Ising spin chains, a lifted toric code, the XXCXXCfamilies of spin chains, and fragmented extensions derived from the integrable H1,11H_1,11and H1,3H_1,3seed densities. The last two models are derived from Hietarinta's classification of constant 4×44\times 4 Yang-Baxter solutions.

item.author: Are Austad, Jonas Eidesen

Abstract:

We associate a spectral triple with each stabilizer code in a projective error model arising from a nice error basis and equipped with a length function. The spectral triple records the dimension of the code as well as the minimum code distance. For Pauli stabilizer codes of dimension greater than one with Hamming weight, Latrémolière's dual propinquity provides a pseudometric which allows us to compare codes of different physical and logical dimensions. We show that in the resulting topology, minimum distance of a code is locally constant for qubits and for qudits of dimensions three and five. Thus correction of all errors up to a prescribed weight is a local property in these cases. Moreover, for each prime pp, we classify the underlying C∗C^*-algebras in the metric closure as a subclass of AF algebras, namely those arising as tensor products of C((Zp)r)C((\mathbb{Z}_p)^r), for r∈{0,1,2,…,∞}r \in \{0,1,2, \ldots , \infty\}, with matrix algebras of pp-power order or the UHF algebra of type p∞p^\infty. item.title: [2★] Every three-qubit pure state admits an equal-modulus expansion in a fixed GHZ basis under local unitaries
item.author: Wei Song, Xiao-Lan Zong
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Wei Song, Xiao-Lan Zong

arXiv ID: 2611.19367 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

In general, local unitary transformations alone do not necessarily generate a complete orthonormal basis from a pure state. We prove that any three-qubit pure state, after suitable local unitary transformations, can be expanded in the same fixed Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger basis, and all expansion coefficients have equal modulus. Thus, eight mutually commuting product reflection operators can generate a complete orthonormal basis from an arbitrary three-qubit pure state, thereby proving the three-qubit commuting-reflection encoding conjecture. We also give two applications of this result: first, using three Bell entanglement links, a pre-specified three-qubit pure state can be deterministically distributed through joint projective measurement and local correction; second, using local random unitary operations, a known pure state can be transformed into a maximally mixed state. The mixing protocol uses a shared three-bit classical label and attains the minimum possible label entropy, even when global unitaries are allowed.

Wei Song, Xiao-Lan Zong

item.title: [2★] Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
item.author: Rathindra Nath Karmakar, Samriddha Lahiry, Koichi Yamagata
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Rathindra Nath Karmakar, Samriddha Lahiry, Koichi Yamagata

arXiv ID: 2611.19141 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

In classical statistics, local asymptotic normality provides a general framework for characterizing optimal testing power and constructing asymptotically efficient procedures. Extending this framework to quantum statistical models introduces additional challenges arising from the noncommutativity of observables and the need to optimize over quantum measurements. In this paper, we develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency for quantum hypothesis testing using quantum local asymptotic normality and the asymptotic representation theorem. We establish sharp nuisance-maximin power bounds for one-sided tests and two-sided tests within the unbiased class by reducing the corresponding classical--quantum Gaussian shift experiments to classical testing problems. This reduction is justified through a quantum Hunt--Stein argument that accommodates both commuting and noncommuting Gaussian coordinates. Under suitable asymptotic invariance conditions, the resulting bounds transfer to the original quantum experiments and are attained by scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests. We further develop a two-stage adaptive construction that achieves the same local asymptotic power without knowledge of the reference parameter. As an application, we study testing of smooth spectral functionals of quantum states. We compare scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests with the weak Schur sampling plug-in test and with optimally weighted linear statistics of its fluctuations. This comparison distinguishes loss from the plug-in weighting from a gap between the best such spectral statistic and the scalar score procedure. We characterize equality of the corresponding variances and illustrate the two gaps through explicit examples.

Rathindra Nath Karmakar, Samriddha Lahiry, Koichi Yamagata

item.title: [2★] Quantum Transitions From Integrable to Chaotic
item.author: Sizhe Yan, Biao Wu
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Sizhe Yan, Biao Wu

arXiv ID: 2611.18777 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The quantum integrable-to-chaotic transition is commonly pictured as the quantum counterpart of the classical Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser (KAM) scenario: a phaseout transition in which a family of regular eigenstates coexists with, and gradually yields to, chaotic eigenstates. Here we show that this is not the only fundamental route from integrability to chaos in quantum systems. We identify a second elementary transition---the morphing transition---which has no classical counterpart: all eigenstates hybridize and turn chaotic concurrently, so that no regular subsequence survives at any stage of the crossover. The two transitions are spectrally distinct: the phaseout spectrum is an independent superposition of regular and chaotic subsequences with Berry-Robnik statistics and a finite short-spacing intercept P(0)P(0), whereas the morphing spectrum exhibits global level repulsion with Lenz-Haake statistics and P(0)=0P(0)=0. We demonstrate both transitions, and their mixture, in three models. The results for the deformed boson model further show that the quantum phaseout scenario is conditional on a smooth quantum-classical correspondence.

Sizhe Yan, Biao Wu

Authors: Benedikt Tissot, Sophia Carmen Simon, Anders Søndberg Sørensen

arXiv ID: 2611.21481 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Ensemble based photonic memories paired with photon pair sources are the essential ingredient for many quantum networking protocols. Most protocols and theoretical analyses focus on networks of identical nodes, however, realistic networks consist of nodes that may vary from device to device. We investigate a network of non-identical memories and develop mitigation strategies for the variation in performance. We find that by strategically distributing the memories among the nodes and individually adapting the emission probabilities based on the memory efficiency the effect of the variance on fidelity and duration can to a large extend be mitigated. Generally, our analysis shows the importance of accounting and compensating for device variations to avoid deteriorating the performance. Lastly, we also link our results to memories where efficiency decays as a function of storage duration. Here, we show that our approach provides a visible improvement for networks with non-identical and decaying memories.

Benedikt Tissot, Sophia Carmen Simon, Anders Søndberg Sørensen

item.title: [1★] Catalytic compression of classical communication in exact entanglement transformations
item.author: Vito Viesti, Alexander Streltsov
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Vito Viesti, Alexander Streltsov

arXiv ID: 2611.21349 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Entanglement catalysis is usually associated with making otherwise impossible transformations possible. Here we show that it can also change how much classical communication a transformation requires. A catalyst, returned exactly and uncorrelated with the output, can reduce the message alphabet size required for exact transformations of bipartite pure states by a factor that grows without bound as the Schmidt rank increases. In the asymptotic many-copy regime, however, this advantage disappears at the level of the leading communication rate: the optimal catalytic and noncatalytic rates coincide. We characterize the optimal catalytic cost in terms of Rényi entropies, revealing how the entanglement structure of the source and target governs the finite-copy advantage. Our results establish reusable entanglement as a resource for compressing classical communication in quantum state manipulation.

Vito Viesti, Alexander Streltsov

item.title: [1★] Quantum adiabatic and diabatic optimization: A Hilbert space engineering strategy with Rydberg arrays
item.author: Rui Lin
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Rui Lin

arXiv ID: 2611.21341 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Neutral-atom arrays provide a versatile platform for encoding combinatorial optimization problems with arbitrary graph connectivity [Nguyen et al., PRX Quantum 4, 010316 (2023)]. Although the dynamics of individual encoding gadgets has been studied [Bombieri et al., PRX Quantum 6, 020306 (2025)], understanding annealing bottlenecks in larger networks remains challenging. We investigate how engineering the Hilbert-space geometry controls quantum annealing in a family of blockaded-chain models motivated by these encodings. While boundary terms encode the target maximum independent set problem, the bulk geometry induces an auxiliary optimization problem associated with independent sets of cliques. Spectrally, the energetics of the quantum system can be approximated by physically derived clique weights. When the target problem and the auxiliary problems are consistent, the low-energy modes lie predominantly within the target subspace. This spectral structure motivates a diabatic annealing strategy that exploits target-compatible excited states, as tested on the diamond-chain graph family. These results provide a framework for predicting annealing bottlenecks, and demonstrate Hilbert-space engineering as a strategy for improving neutral-atom quantum optimization protocols.

Rui Lin

item.title: [1★] Experimentally relevant witness for non-Markovianity in discrete time crystals
item.author: Rahul Ghosh, Victor Mukherjee, Yonatan Dubi
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Rahul Ghosh, Victor Mukherjee, Yonatan Dubi

arXiv ID: 2611.21332 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Discrete time crystals (DTCs) are almost always analyzed under the Born-Markov approximation, in which the environment is memoryless. We show that a reservoir with a finite correlation time τm\tau_m leaves an exact and strikingly simple imprint on the stroboscopic dynamics of DTCs, which can be used as an experimentally relevant witness for non-Markovianity. By analyzing a post-Markovian master equation we prove that the Floquet spectrum splits into the ordinary Markovian spectrum plus a replica of the purely unitary Floquet spectrum, uniformly contracted by e−T/τme^{-T/\tau_m}, where TT is the drive period. Consequently, the DTC signal decay rate becomes independent of any system parameter once τm\tau_m exceeds the Markovian lifetime of the DTC. The measured decay, and in particular its insensitivity to tunable system parameters, thus becomes a direct read-out of the reservoir correlation time. Below this threshold the dynamics is already non-Markovian, but the memory remains hidden in the decay. We confirm this in two structurally unrelated DTCs, a collective long-range model with incoherent pumping and a disorder-free Ising chain with dephasing, where a single estimator recovers τm\tau_m. The time crystal thereby witnesses the non-Markovianity of its own environment.

Rahul Ghosh, Victor Mukherjee, Yonatan Dubi

item.title: [1★] SCOPE: A Physical Execution Latency-Guided Quantum Circuit Compilation Framework
item.author: Bolin Zhang, ..., Jiandong Shang, Qiang Chen
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Bolin Zhang, ..., Jiandong Shang, Qiang Chen

arXiv ID: 2611.21270 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum computing requires compilers to translate algorithms represented in the quantum circuit model into unitary operations supported by physical devices. Limited coherence time makes physical execution latency an important compilation objective. Gate fusion can shorten pulses, but gate count and depth do not capture fused targets' control demands. Evaluating every candidate with quantum optimal control (QOC) would embed pulse optimization in structural search. We present Schmidt-guided Compilation for Optimized Pulse Execution (SCOPE), driven by an operator Schmidt time surrogate. The target's angular distance from product operators measures the required nonlocal change; dividing it by a coupling-limited evolution-rate bound gives a lower bound on exact implementation time. Trace-angle and waveform constraints complete block scores for critical-path evaluation during genetic search. Local QOC determines final pulse durations. Under a numerical nearest-neighbor control model, all 104 results across 13 instances from four application families have shorter QOC critical-path durations than an adapted efficient pulse generation framework with advanced synthesis for quantum circuits (EPOC). Using eight-run instance means, the equally weighted reduction is 42.50\%, with a geometric mean speedup of 2.00. In a shared six-qubit quantum Fourier transform (QFT) ablation, time-surrogate guidance reduces mean QOC duration by 22.21\% relative to gate-count guidance and 21.01\% relative to depth guidance, validating the surrogate's joint use in fitness evaluation and mutation-region selection.

Bolin Zhang, ..., Jiandong Shang, Qiang Chen

item.title: [1★] Relaxing the i.i.d. state preparation assumption with the block QKD protocol
item.author: Olgierd Żurek, Hoi-Kwong Lo
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Olgierd Żurek, Hoi-Kwong Lo

arXiv ID: 2611.21048 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

In this work, we propose a novel approach to handling the independent and identically distributed assumption for the state preparation in prepare-and measure QKD protocols. Contrary to previous approaches, we do not prove the security using sub-protocols, and instead opt to guarantee security in the presence of correlations by dividing the communication into finite blocks of consecutive pulses, and adding an additional assumption of no dependence between each block. In turn we obtain a protocol which uses only a relaxed i.i.d. assumption and is easier to implement than subprotocol-style approaches since it does not require separate statistics for each sub-protocol, whose number grows with the correlation length of the underlying dependency.

Olgierd Żurek, Hoi-Kwong Lo

item.title: [1★] Quantum Sensor of Mechanical Vibrations
item.author: Mu Young Kim, ..., Nigel Benjamin Lee Junsheng, Dzmitry Matsukevich
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Mu Young Kim, ..., Nigel Benjamin Lee Junsheng, Dzmitry Matsukevich

arXiv ID: 2611.20610 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We report the use of a single trapped-ion motional mode as a probe of mechanical vibrations of the Paul trap structure. By exciting vibrations of the trap using an ultrasonic transducer mounted outside the vacuum chamber and probing the ion motion through motional sideband interactions, we observe a clear resonance response of the axial mode. We further demonstrate detection of trap vibrations with amplitudes as low as 0.6 picometers. These measurements show direct coupling between macroscopic mechanical motion and trapped-ion dynamics, providing a route toward vibration sensing using quantum control of motional states.

Mu Young Kim, ..., Nigel Benjamin Lee Junsheng, Dzmitry Matsukevich

item.title: [1★] Postselection on Halting and Reductions to the Halting Problem
item.author: Saman Farhat, Farzad Didehvar
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Saman Farhat, Farzad Didehvar

arXiv ID: 2611.20517 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

A probabilistic Turing machine is an ordinary Turing machine that may also toss fair coins, with no limit on its running time or memory. If it always halts, it decides only computable problems. Aaronson et al. studied machines that may run forever on some coin tosses, with the answer read only from the runs that halt. Suppose the correct answer must be more than twice as likely as the wrong one. They showed that these machines decide exactly the problems solvable with a fixed list of questions about the halting problem. They asked what happens when the correct answer need only be the more likely one. We show that the machines then decide exactly the problems solvable by asking such questions one after another, each chosen after the earlier answers. We also show that the factor two can be replaced by any fixed factor greater than one. A machine may promise two numbers: a lower bound on its probability of halting, and a lower bound on its probability of being right when it halts. From these two numbers we compute exactly how many questions fixed in advance the machine can replace. The main idea is that probability acts as a budget for how often a computable guess may change its mind. The results extend to oracle machines and to machines nested inside each other. Quantum machines decide the same problems.

Saman Farhat, Farzad Didehvar

item.title: [1★] Lieb-Robinson Bounds for Electric Quantum Walks
item.author: Houssam Abdul-Rahman, Christopher Cedzich, Günter Stolz
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Houssam Abdul-Rahman, Christopher Cedzich, Günter Stolz

arXiv ID: 2611.20516 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We derive Lieb-Robinson type bounds with optimal propagation velocity for shift-coin and split-step quantum walks in rational electric fields. The velocity decays exponentially fast in the period of the field, showing long intervals of suppressed spreading. The proof rests on bounds for the imaginary part of the analytically continued dispersion relation of the electric walk. We show that the infimal Lieb-Robinson velocity coincides with the asymptotic velocity for these walks, while a nonhomogeneous example demonstrates that the two types of velocity need not agree in general. We also obtain an exponential tail estimate on the probability of a walk to lie outside the effective light cone.

Houssam Abdul-Rahman, Christopher Cedzich, Günter Stolz

item.title: [1★] Quantum geometric spectroscopy with Schrödinger cat states
item.author: Shohei Imai, Marcelo F. Ciappina
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Shohei Imai, Marcelo F. Ciappina

arXiv ID: 2611.20434 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We propose a spectroscopic approach that reads out the quantum geometry of matter from the quantum decoherence of Schrödinger-cat light, in the same way that optical absorption reads out the energy structure of matter. For a cat-state probe comprising a superposition of two coherent states, the interbranch coherence of the outgoing light encodes the overlap between the matter states driven by the two branches. We show that, when the electromagnetic fields of the two branches differ only slightly, cat-branch decoherence is quantified by dynamical quantum geometry, which characterizes infinitesimal displacements on the matter-state manifold. For frequency-selective kitten probes of equilibrium matter, we further establish a partition law for the quantum geometric tensor between light and matter, enabling optical readout of matter quantum metric and Berry curvature through, for example, the brightening of a stellar zero in the outgoing Husimi function. For nonequilibrium matter in a pure state, short-pulse cat probes also provide a time-resolved witness of multipartite entanglement through the transient quantum metric, which can be extracted from homodyne measurements of the outgoing light. By turning cat-state decoherence, conventionally regarded as a loss of quantum information, into a carrier of information about matter, this approach establishes a spectroscopic principle that directly probes quantum-state geometry and fluctuations alongside conventional response-based spectroscopy.

Shohei Imai, Marcelo F. Ciappina

item.title: [1★] A Forward Bit Makes Error Correction Dispensable for Antidegradable Amplitude-Damping Channels
item.author: Ahmed Gamal, ..., Kazunori Ueda, Ahmed El-Mahdy
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Ahmed Gamal, ..., Kazunori Ueda, Ahmed El-Mahdy

arXiv ID: 2611.20118 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Preserving a qubit usually relies on redundant encoding over many uses of a noisy channel. We prove that for antidegradable amplitude damping, one channel use with one forward classical bit matches or beats every forward-assisted or unassisted code with any number of uses. We then show that variational circuits learn to switch from error correction to classical assistance as damping grows, beating a dual-certified bound on all unassisted three-use codes and, relative to the best unassisted see-saw, extending storage time by up to 13% at entanglement fidelity down to 0.65.

Ahmed Gamal, ..., Kazunori Ueda, Ahmed El-Mahdy

item.title: [1★] Efficient AOD-Transport Compilation for Neutral-Atom Arrays
item.author: Haydn Cheng, Zhiding Liang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Haydn Cheng, Zhiding Liang

arXiv ID: 2611.19994 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Neutral-atom quantum computers execute two-qubit gates by shuttling atoms between storage and entanglement zones with acousto-optic deflectors (AODs). The efficiency of these movements determines circuit fidelity via transport overhead, idle-atom crosstalk, and atom-transfer errors. Additionally, AOD hardware constraints limit parallel atom movements, so efficient qubit placement and routing are essential. We present NEAT (Neutral-atom Efficient AOD-Transport compiler). Its transport-informed placement evaluates each decision by its incremental equivalent time, a single cost combining transport time, atom-transfer loss, and crosstalk. Its partial-progress routing allows conflicting moves to advance concurrently via intermediate waypoints. NEAT also schedules gates to maximize parallelism and uses a staggered atom array whose trap geometry preemptively avoids AOD violations without extra moves. On standard benchmark circuits, NEAT outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) compilers in fidelity, circuit duration, and compilation time. On scalability benchmarks of up to 1,000 qubits, it shortens circuits by 1.9x, reduces the negative log-fidelity by 1.5x, and compiles 6.6x faster than SOTA compilers on average. Overall, NEAT is a lightweight yet effective compiler for efficient and scalable neutral-atom quantum computing. The code is available at https://github.com/HaydnCheng77/NEAT.

Haydn Cheng, Zhiding Liang

item.title: [1★] Pulse-timing errors in exchange-only spin qubits: how one control imperfection propagates to VQE, QAOA and fault-tolerance primitives
item.author: Yuichiro Minato
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Yuichiro Minato

arXiv ID: 2611.19986 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

In an exchange-only (EO) spin qubit every gate is a sequence of Heisenberg exchange pulses whose only continuous parameter is the pulse area. We ask how an error in that area propagates to an algorithm's result. On up to six encoded qubits we compile VQE for H22_2 and LiH, QAOA MaxCut, Grover search, phase estimation and a distance-3 repetition code into exchange pulses and perturb every pulse with a systematic fractional error ε\varepsilon, an offset or per-pulse jitter. For circuits whose first-order response is negligible at the threshold, the useful regime ends at ε\varepsilon of a few 10−310^{-3}: chemical accuracy is lost at ≈6×10−3\approx6\times10^{-3} for both molecules and 5% of success probability between 3 and 9×10−39\times10^{-3} for 498-1216 pulses. A systematic error accumulates as the square of the depth and biases the answer; jitter accumulates linearly and, within statistics, does not bias phase estimation. Leakage from inter-block pulses is a third of the CNOT error, survives variational re-optimisation and a leakage-controlled entangler, and makes a leakage-blind repetition-code round worse than its uncorrected data by a factor 38-93 at ε=10−2\varepsilon=10^{-2} in three of four compilations; in the fourth the uncorrected data already fail. The compilation moves the thresholds by a factor of two to eight. Measured over-rotation and exchange noise put devices at the edge of this regime, and with the measured 3.5 μ\mus T∗2T_2^* a quasi-static magnetic gradient limits thousand-pulse circuits unless J/hJ/h reaches several hundred MHz with continuous areas, because a duration grid of 2-5% of the SWAP time starts to cost chemical accuracy. As a bit budget, a common-mode area error needs 8-10 significant bits and a 6-bit significand for the durations suffices in the tested circuits; half-precision words and picosecond timers exceed this; older devices had 6-8 bits of analog stability.

Yuichiro Minato

item.title: [1★] Efficient numerical measurement design and certified risk bounds for multiparameter quantum estimation
item.author: Koichi Yamagata, Wataru Ikeura
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Koichi Yamagata, Wataru Ikeura

arXiv ID: 2611.19814 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Multiparameter quantum estimation requires efficient measurement design and reliable bounds on the attainable precision. We present Q-StARC, a numerical framework that combines measurement optimization with certified lower bounds on the weighted variance of locally unbiased estimators. The measurement search parameterizes rank-one measurements on a complex Stiefel manifold and combines projected ambient Adam updates, QR retraction, and Riemannian conjugate-gradient refinement. Independent risk bounds are obtained from a denominator-based matrix sum-of-squares hierarchy. When its support coefficients are optimized jointly, the hierarchy starts at the weighted Nagaoka-Hayashi (NH) bound and converges to the optimal locally unbiased risk, including for singular states. Numerical applications certify that the NH bound is unattainable for several finite-copy qubit models and two full eight-parameter qutrit models. For the qutrit examples, the certified relative gaps above the NH bound exceed 14%14\% and 11%11\%, while the level-m=1m=1 lower bounds agree with the best numerical measurement costs to relative differences of 4.5×10−74.5\times10^{-7} and 2.2×10−62.2\times10^{-6}, respectively.

Koichi Yamagata, Wataru Ikeura

item.author: Cong Xu, ..., Qing-Hua Zhang, Shao-Ming Fei
